clue.text: Graduate entering African state linked with Trinidad

indicators.note: the graduate's letters go into the middle of the African country's name

parts.note: Togo is a country in West Africa
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate moves to an African country that has ties with Trinidad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the container. The definition leans on Trinidad, its partner island in one Caribbean republic.
explanation.definitionFit: The island forms one twin-island republic together with Trinidad in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Old man was employed, but didn't keep going

parts.note: an old man is slang for a father, PA
was employed means was used

explanation.surface: An elderly man had a job but stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop for a moment is not to carry on.

clue.text: The trouble with people who see things only in black and white

definitions.text: The trouble with people who see things only in black and white

parts.words: The trouble with people who see things only in black and white
parts.note: seeing things only in black and white usually means being rigid in opinion, but here it is taken literally as a visual defect where hues cannot be told apart

explanation.surface: A complaint about narrow-minded people who cannot see nuance.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual condition in which hues are hard to tell apart literally leaves a person seeing in monochrome.

clue.text: Free advice to satisfied tenant whose term has expired

definitions.meaning: to free is to let go or liberate

definitions.text: advice to satisfied tenant whose term has expired
definitions.meaning: a happy renter at the end of a contract would be told to rent the place again

explanation.definitionFit: To set loose means to free; split as re-lease it is the counsel to sign the rental agreement again.

clue.text: UN concentrating one on friendly state by accident

parts.note: concentrating means intent, focused
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
a friendly state is an ally

explanation.surface: The United Nations focuses on a country, by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentrating' is the adjective intent, not the verb; the long answer splits neatly into five short words read in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without meaning to is doing it by chance or mishap.

clue.text: Full of beans or full of gin?

definitions.meaning: full of beans means lively and energetic
gin is a spirit, so something full of it is jokingly filled with spirits

explanation.definitionFit: Lively people are full of beans; gin being a spirit, the word also jokingly describes something filled with liquor.

clue.text: The macho attitude of Parisian boy friend

parts.note: the French for 'of' is de, as a Parisian would say it
a boy friend who has proposed is a fiance

explanation.surface: Describing the masculine swagger of a Frenchman's boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold, challenging stance of resistance is a show of macho attitude.

clue.text: State from which we see a drunken sot come around?

indicators.note: a drunken person reels about, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking what condition a drunkard who comes round has been in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' is the anagram signal. The surface plays on a sot coming round from a stupor, which is the very state defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep unconscious condition is a state from which a person may come round.

clue.text: Young lad who pinches

definitions.meaning: a young lad is a small boy
something that pinches or nips, like a crab's claw

explanation.definitionFit: A small boy is colloquially called this, and the word also means one that nips or squeezes.

clue.text: Flowery tribute from a fertile isle

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A floral gift brought from a lush island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland of blossoms given as a welcome is a floral tribute.

clue.text: Mews house?

parts.note: a mews is a row of converted stables, but 'mew' is also a feline's cry, so a house of mewing creatures

explanation.surface: A question about a converted stable dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A mews is a British row of former stables turned into homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mewing animals' dwelling is a playful reading of a mews house.

clue.text: Scandinavian police depart, ment Mr Todd upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns things over, here reading the joined pieces backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
Ron Todd was a well-known British trade-union leader

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian police force has upset a man named Todd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CID and RON over together, giving NOR + DIC. Ron Todd led the Transport and General Workers' Union in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers the peoples and lands of northern Europe such as Norway and Sweden.

clue.text: The glittering outlook in preparing long dig

indicators.note: in places the view word inside the rearranged letters
preparing suggests the letters are being worked into a new form

parts.note: an outlook is a prospect, a view of the future

explanation.surface: A bright future lies in getting ready for a lengthy excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparing' rearranges the letters of LONG DIG into GOLDING, and 'in' sets the outlook word after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching for the yellow metal is literally hunting for what glitters.

clue.text: Cheek by jowl

definitions.meaning: the jowl is the jaw area, and the mouth's edge lies beside it

explanation.definitionFit: Impudent talk is called cheek, and the mouth's fleshy edge lies near the jowl.

clue.text: Place US reserved for astronauts' accommodation

indicators.note: read as re-served, served up again in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spot in America set aside for spacemen's quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft's crew compartment is a small sealed pod for space travellers.

clue.text: Renegade who rids a police state of parasites

indicators.note: rids X of Y means removing the pests from the run of words

parts.note: taken as written
lice are parasites

explanation.surface: A rebel frees an authoritarian country of its pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rids ... of' takes LICE out of A POLICE STATE, leaving A PO STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat abandons a faith or cause, which is what a renegade does.

clue.text: Bet lusty disposition militates against it

definitions.text: Bet lusty disposition militates against it

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wager that a lusty temperament works against finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' rearranges BET LUSTY. The whole clue also says that a lusty nature works against the quality defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicacy and finesse are what a coarse, lusty temperament tends to lack.

clue.text: Sketches for reading rooms

definitions.meaning: rooms in a house for reading and working

explanation.definitionFit: Preparatory drawings by artists share the name with private rooms set aside for work and reading.

clue.text: Japanese sash upset one from Nigeria

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned over, read from bottom up

parts.note: an obi is the sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: A kimono belt knocked over by a Nigerian.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a West African people of south-eastern Nigeria, also spelt Igbo.

clue.text: Furniture use in Sunday school for keeping chargers

indicators.note: use in tells us to put the piece of furniture within the abbreviation

parts.note: S for Sunday and S for school
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Putting furniture into a Sunday school building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use in' is the container signal; Sunday school gives two separate S abbreviations, and chargers are war-horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Buildings for horses house the war-horses called chargers.

clue.text: The key to it should be kept in mind

definitions.text: The key to it should be kept in mind

parts.words: The key to it should be kept in mind
parts.note: the key here is not metal but a sequence of numbers that must be memorised to open the fastening

explanation.surface: Advice to remember the essentials of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastening opened by a remembered code needs no physical key.

clue.text: Rulers of the mercantile fleet

definitions.meaning: rulers are things that draw lines
large passenger ships of a merchant line

explanation.definitionFit: Straight-edges that rule lines share the word with big passenger ships of a shipping company.

clue.text: Maybe a beer for the speed cop

definitions.meaning: a beer drunk after spirits to follow them down
a traffic officer who pursues speeding drivers

explanation.definitionFit: A drink following a shot is a follow-up drink, and a police officer pursuing speeders is a pursuer.

clue.text: Point to scarf taken during burglary

indicators.note: to means the compass letter is attached to the end of the scarf

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A thief points at a scarf grabbed in a break-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried off by a burglar are pilfered property.

clue.text: What the homicidal prefect may do from mental exhaustion

definitions.text: What the homicidal prefect may do
definitions.meaning: a murderous senior pupil might bash the skull of his fag, the junior boy who serves him at a British boarding school
an old term for nervous tiredness

explanation.walkthrough: At British public schools a fag was a junior pupil who ran errands for a senior, and a prefect was a senior pupil with authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang for being worn out by too much thinking; split, it reads as a violent act on a junior pupil.

clue.text: Material measure suggested by English Liberals

parts.note: L for Liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A measurement proposed by English Liberal politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An old unit of length used for cloth, about forty-five inches.

clue.text: Rank which is socially acceptable in statistics

indicators.note: in puts the class letter inside the word for figures

parts.note: stats is short for statistics
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A position that is respectable according to the figures.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and non-upper-class British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing or position in society is one's rank.

clue.text: Made very big in the end

definitions.text: Made very big in the end

indicators.note: in places the word for big inside the word for finish

parts.note: taken as the word end
large means very big

explanation.surface: Something that grew huge eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, and the whole clue reads as both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something increased in size has been made bigger.
